description: Message signing vectors from the Bitcoin Core test suite (unit and functional tests), and the verification vectors of its message_verify unit test.

vectors.name: bitcoin-core/unit/message_sign
vectors.comment: Compressed key set from raw bytes. The address comes from the comment in the test.

vectors.name: bitcoin-core/functional/signmessagewithprivkey
vectors.message: This is just a test message
vectors.comment: Regtest WIF key and P2PKH address. Regtest uses the testnet address and WIF prefixes.

verification.name: bitcoin-core/verify/p2sh-address
verification.comment: ERR_ADDRESS_NO_KEY: a P2SH address has no key to sign with. The signature is not even read.

verification.name: bitcoin-core/verify/not-base64
verification.signature: invalid signature, not in base64 encoding
verification.comment: ERR_MALFORMED_SIGNATURE: the signature is not base64.

verification.name: bitcoin-core/verify/zero-signature
verification.comment: ERR_PUBKEY_NOT_RECOVERED: 65 zero bytes. The header byte 0 is outside 27 to 34, and r = 0 is outside the curve order: no key can be recovered, so the signature is not valid for any address.

verification.name: bitcoin-core/verify/not-signed
verification.comment: ERR_NOT_SIGNED: the signature of "Trust no one" (the message_sign vector) checked against another message recovers another key.

verification.name: bitcoin-core/verify/ok
verification.comment: The signature of the message_sign vector, verified.

verification.name: bitcoin-core/verify/crafted
verification.comment: A crafted signature: r and s are the text "Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks" with padding, and the address is the one of the key they recover. Nobody holds that key, yet the signature is valid: the verifier can only check that the recovered key is the key of the address.
